title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche, section-conjecture chapter). U is a hyperbolic curve over a field K of finite type over Q. X = Û is its smooth compactification, and I = X̄ − Ū is the set of cusps. Ũ is the universal (pro-)étale cover of U, X' is the normalization of X in Ũ, E_U = π_1(U), E_K = Gal(K̄/K) = Γ, and π̄ = π_1(Ū). On the previous page the fibres X'_i over a cusp i were identified with the conjugacy classes L_i of 'loop subgroups' (inertia, cuspidal subgroups) of π̄. So X' = Ũ ∪ {points at infinity}, i.e. the cuspidally compactified universal cover.

This page:
(1) E_U is read as the group of U-automorphisms of the scheme Ũ. E_U → E_K is the map induced on K̄, because K̄ is the algebraic closure of K in H^0(Ũ, O). So E_U acts naturally on Spec K̄.
(2) A section s: E_K → E_U is therefore the same as an action of Γ on Ũ that lifts the Galois action on K̄ and is continuous. G. suggests the continuity is something like 'uniform discrete convergence' on the finite intermediate covers Ũ_i between U and Ũ.
(3) Conjecture B: every such action has exactly one fixed point in X' = Ũ^ (the compactified universal cover). The margin adds that the same should hold for the induced action of an open subgroup Γ° ('cf plus bas').
(4) Unpacking, case a): suppose there is a fixed point at finite distance, x̃ ∈ Ũ^Γ. Then:
- 1° its image in U is unique. This is the injectivity of U(K) → {sections}/conjugacy proved in §1.
- 2° (next page) π̄^Γ = 1, i.e. the centralizer of the section in π̄ is trivial, so x̃ is the only fixed point above x.
- 3° there is no fixed point at infinity: no L_i is normalized by Γ.
(5) Case b) (next page): suppose the fixed point is at infinity.
- Uniqueness of the image in X means a section cannot normalize L_i and L_j for i ≠ j. This is established except for (g,ν) = (0,3).
- Uniqueness over a fixed i means the normalized L_i is unique. This weakens the earlier conjecture L_i = Cen π̄^{Γ°}.

What the page achieves: it recasts the (cuspidal) section conjecture as a fixed-point theorem for Galois actions on the compactified universal cover. Sections correspond bijectively to X(K)-type data: rational points plus cuspidal packets. The page also splits the bijectivity into injectivity, trivial-centralizer and disjointness statements.
errors: No mathematical error. The definition of 'continuous action' is left vague; G. himself marks it as tentative ('sans doute ...').
Uniqueness of fixed points for all open Γ° (margin) is a strictly stronger, hereditary statement. It is not deduced, just asserted as part of the expected picture.

The rational-cusp case is subtle. Over a K-rational cusp there is a whole packet of cuspidal sections (parametrized by H^1(K, Ẑ(1)) ≅ (K^*)^). Each fixes a different point of X' above i, so 'one fixed point' is per section, not per cusp. The page is consistent with this, but does not spell it out.

ideas.what: Sections of π_1(U) → Gal_K identified with continuous semilinear Γ-actions on the universal pro-cover Ũ
ideas.modern_name: Sections as Galois actions on the universal pro-étale cover / decomposition groups of pro-points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); standard in Stix, Rational Points and Arithmetic of Fundamental Groups (LNM 2054)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983), in Geometric Galois Actions vol. 1

ideas.what: Conjecture B: every section has exactly one fixed point in the normalization X' of X in Ũ, cusps included as 'points at infinity'
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture with cuspidal sections (fixed-point formulation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1983; cuspidal sections studied by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Stix, Esnault–Hai
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (sketched); the fixed-point-on-compactified-cover phrasing is more explicit here

ideas.what: Decomposition of bijectivity into: injectivity on U(K); trivial centralizer π̄^Γ = 1; no section both 'finite' and cuspidal; a section normalizes at most one cuspidal inertia class; uniqueness of the normalized L_i
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the section map, triviality of centralizers of sections, separation of cuspidal decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Injectivity: Grothendieck / Mordell–Weil–Kummer argument (Stix); cuspidal separation: Nakamura, Tamagawa (1997)

ideas.what: Hereditary version: uniqueness of fixed points for every open subgroup Γ°
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture for all finite extensions / neighbourhoods of a section

missed.claim: An explicit fixed-point formulation of the cuspidal section conjecture on the compactified universal cover X' (with cusps as 'points at infinity' = loop subgroups). It comes with an elementwise breakdown and a candidate topology ('uniform discrete convergence on finite intermediate covers') for continuity of semilinear actions. This is essentially what later literature does, but it documents that Grothendieck had the cuspidal and centralizer parts worked out in detail.
missed.quote: Toute telle action de Γ sur Ũ admet dans X' = Û un pt fixe et un seul.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows the cuspidal-section and trivial-centralizer aspects, later credited to others, were explicit in Grothendieck's notes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean geometric reformulation of the section conjecture including cusps, matching the 1983 Faltings letter and later standard treatments (Stix). The breakdown into sub-statements is a nice documented detail, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Margin probably reads 'et ∀ Γ° l'action induite de Γ° doit avoir un pt fixe et un seul — cf plus bas' (Γ° = open subgroup, consistent with π^{Γ^0} on the next page), not 'une telle action induite de Γ'.
'sur les ... Ū_i finis sur Ū entre Ū et Ũ' is likely 'sur les Ũ_i finis sur U entre U et Ũ' (finite intermediate covers).
'induit [?] ... K̄ s'identifie' — reads as '(passage au quotient) induit, vu que K̄ s'identifie à la clôture alg. de K dans H^0(Ũ, O_Ũ)'.
